given: a warehouse operator is filing a stock record for a SKU at a location
when: the filed quantity is below zero
then: the filing is rejected with a clear message that names the quantity field, and no stock record is created or changed
architectural_notes: API boundary: the filing POST enters app/routes/ (boundary) -> app/services/ (business logic) -> app/repositories/ -> app/models/. The negative-quantity rejection is a write-time guard owned by the service layer (business rule 'no negative stock', NFR-F1-2/brief_ref R2), defended in depth by PI3 (CHECK quantity >= 0 on stock_records); on rejection the boundary returns a field-named error identifying the quantity field and no row is created or changed. This names the QUANTITY field specifically and is DISTINCT from NFR-F1-6's missing/blank-required-field validation (SKU/tracking code), which is exercised via AC1's boundary validation and its own behavior test. Verified against the paired branch (NFR-F1-4).

independence.rationale: This asserts the write-time rejection of a negative quantity with a field-naming message, an outcome independently breakable from the happy-path create (AC1) and the collision update (AC2): an implementation can persist and update correctly yet still accept a negative quantity or reject it with an unnamed error.
